chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from the wife of Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The shouting/crying out upon the deceased is not befitting, nor is tearing of the clothes.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on crying loudly and tearing clothes during mourning in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the Sunnah of dignified mourning by prohibiting 'siyah' (loud wailing) and 'shaqq' (tearing garments), practices common in pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah that implied dissatisfaction with divine decree. This ruling is deeply connected to the verse 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' (2:156), as it encourages believers to embody patience (sabr) and acceptance rather than the frantic despair characteristic of the ignorant. By restraining outward displays of excessive grief, the believer affirms trust in Allah's return of the soul, aligning physical conduct with spiritual submission.
